result.title: Plausible Videos Can Lead to Poor Decisions: Diagnosing and CURE-ing World Models for Planning
result.summary: Action-conditioned world models are increasingly used as world models for planning, yet a world model that makes plausible, realistic-looking videos that are consistent with the training data can produce poor decisions. We address two key questions: (1) when can we trust a world model for planning, and (2) what should we do when we cannot? We introduce CURE (Certify, Upweight, Rollout, Explore), a certificate-guided technique that assesses whether a world model can be trusted for planning and determines what to do next: whether to upweight the training data to debias the model; roll out more samples at test time; or explore by collecting new data where support (how well the training data cover the planner's decisions) is missing. We deploy CURE across multiple domains, spanning simulated physics based on PhyWorld, MuJoCo arm control, and Language-Table pushing in simulation and on real videos. The decisions our certificate trusts have lower regret than those it does not (e.g., 0.06 vs. 0.38 on Language-Table sim and 0.07 vs. 0.38 on MuJoCo contact), whereas video perceptual quality does not identify good decisions. By focusing on decision quality rather than perceptual quality, CURE lowers regret over the best pessimistic decision rule by 10-25% across support levels, and over world-action models, search and policy learning by 41-64%, given the same data.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CURE：先用「证书」评估 action-conditioned world model 能否可信地用于规划，再根据缺失的 support 决定对训练数据重加权、测试时增加 rollout 采样，还是主动采集新数据；在 PhyWorld、MuJoCo 与 Language-Table（含真机视频）上验证了决策 regret 与视频感知质量并不一致。
AI.relevance_reason: 「生成画面逼真≠内部状态可用于决策」这一诊断，与 LVR 中 latent/视觉证据是否保留任务必要信息的问题同构；其可信度证书、support 覆盖判断以及「何时多采样、何时停取证据」的决策规则，可能为 latent 推理中的停止决策与证据获取提供可供核查的表述。
